title: Word 20 — On the Struggle Against Sin
attribution_note: Word 20 of 28 in the collection Short Moral-Instructive Words — see Word 1 for provenance.

pairs.en: All Christians who wish to be true Christians and to obtain eternal salvation in Christ Jesus must without fail carry on a struggle against every sin, lest it come to rule over them. *“Let not sin reign in your mortal body, that you should obey it in its lusts,”* says the Apostle to Christians [Romans 6:12]. Their faith demands this of them, according to the Apostle's word: *“show me your faith by your works”* [James 2:18]. They must listen to God, in whom they believe, and not to sin, and live for God, and not for sin. Holy Baptism demands this, by which they were renewed for holy Christian life. The vows given at Baptism demand this, by which they promised to serve the Lord in faith and truth. The work of salvation demands this, since for those who break the law and do not keep the vows given at Baptism, holy Baptism is of no use — they are liars who have lied to God. Consider this well, Christians.

A Christian is known not by the words *“Lord, Lord,”* but by the struggle against every sin. He is a true soldier who stands and fights against a visible enemy. So too the true Christian is the one who unceasingly carries on the struggle against sin.

sections.heading: Five Causes of Sin, Part One

pairs.en: 2) The devil leads man into sin. Of this the Apostle speaks, warning Christians to be on guard against him: *“Be sober, be vigilant, because your adversary the devil walks about like a roaring lion, seeking whom he may devour.* *Resist him, steadfast in the faith”* [1 Peter 5:8–9]. The Apostle Paul says the same elsewhere: *“Be strong in the Lord and in the power of His might.* *Put on the whole armor of God, that you may be able to stand against the wiles of the devil; for we wrestle not against flesh and blood, but against principalities, against powers, against the rulers of the darkness of this age, against spiritual wickedness in high places”* [Ephesians 6:10–12]. These unseen enemies, O Christians, are ever watchful for our ruin, and strive to lead us into every sin. So we too must not slumber.

sections.heading: Five Causes of Sin, Part Two

pairs.en: 5) Human habit draws powerfully toward sin. We see this evil — drunkards always drawn to drunkenness, thieves to theft, fornicators and adulterers to uncleanness, slanderers to slander, and so on. For their habit draws them to sin like a rope, and as the hungry man is drawn to bread and the thirsty to water, so they are drawn to the sin to which they have grown accustomed. Goaded by habit, people sin. Against habit the Christian who wishes to be saved and to show his faith by his works must without fail struggle.

sections.heading: The Fierce Enemies and the Difficulty of the Struggle

pairs.en: Fierce are all these adversaries of our salvation. Fierce is *“the flesh with its passions and lusts”* [Galatians 5:24], which *“lusts against the Spirit”* [Galatians 5:17]; fierce is our foe the devil, who ceaselessly deceives and wars against us; fierce too are the temptations by which fleshly desire is fanned and kindled like fire in the wind. But for one grown accustomed to evil, fiercest of all is habit, which becomes for him a second nature.

I confess the struggle against these adversaries described above is hard for everyone, but it is necessary and honorable. Many struggle and conquer other men, yet become captives and slaves of their own passions. There is no more glorious victory than to conquer oneself and sin. There is no crown and no triumph without victory, and no victory without struggle against the enemy.
Beloved Christians! Let us enter into this struggle, that with the help of Christ we may win the victory, and receive from Him the crown of goodness, and triumph forever in His kingdom.

sections.heading: Aids in the Struggle, Part One

pairs.en: 3) To remember the end: death, the judgment of Christ, hell, and the heavenly kingdom — all this turns one away from sin. *“In all your deeds,”* says Sirach, *“remember your end, and you will never sin”* [Sirach 7:39 (LXX)].

sections.heading: Aids in the Struggle, Part Two

pairs.en: 7) Not to look at what other people do, but to heed what the Word of God teaches. For thus we turn aside from the temptations of the world. *“Great peace have they who love Your law, O Lord, and nothing shall offend them”* [Psalm 118:165 (LXX)]. Christian, love the Law of God, and the temptations of the world shall not harm you.

8) Our striving and our struggle against sin have no power without the help of God. Therefore we must strive and pray that the Lord will help us in so important a work. God helps those who strive and take care, strengthens those who struggle, and crowns those who conquer.

Beloved Christians! We see our spiritual enemies, who wish to destroy us not for a time but forever, and we see also the help available in the struggle against them. Let us stand, then — let us stand firm, and be strengthened by the power of the almighty Jesus, our Savior, and not allow them to rule over us; then we too shall be crowned with the crown of victory by Jesus, the Author of our struggle! Lord Jesus, Conqueror of death and hell, help us! Without You we can do nothing; with You we can do all things. Amen.
